documentation: There is no generic kotlin.math.* → Lua math.* binding mechanism — only 5 names have real, specific codegen in Emitter.kt's emitCall; everything else falls through to a literal same-name Lua call and fails at runtime. import kotlin.math.* itself is a parsed no-op (wildcard imports are dropped) — it doesn't enable anything.

declarations.name: sqrt
declarations.documentation: Called as a top-level free function sqrt(x), not Double.sqrt — compiles to math.sqrt(x)

declarations.name: abs
declarations.documentation: Top-level call abs(x) → math.abs(x); same codegen used for the Int overload too

declarations.name: max
limitations: Fixed 2-positional-argument arity only; no vararg maxOf(...) overload, no named arguments

declarations.name: pow
limitations: Real Kotlin calls this as a method, x.pow(2) — there is no .pow() method dispatch at all. Only a non-idiomatic top-level pow(a, b) is recognized, which compiles to (a ^ b); idiomatic x.pow(2) is a genuine gap, not just a limitation

declarations.name: floor
limitations: No dedicated top-level codegen (math.floor is only ever emitted internally by the Int/Int truncating-division helper __intdiv, never reachable from user Kotlin source) — falls through to an undefined-global call and fails at runtime

declarations.name: ceil
limitations: Same as floor() — math.ceil only appears internally, never reachable from user source

declarations.name: PI
limitations: Falls through to an undefined global PI, not Lua's math.pi
